description: §17.6.10 — the VALUE-FORM: an `if` that is the sole content of a markup `${…}` interpolation, every branch exactly one expression, renders the selected branch's value. `#out-admin` takes the true branch ('Admin'), `#out-guest` the false branch ('User'). `#out-lift` writes the SAME shape with an explicit `lift` in each branch and renders identically — pinning the §17.6.10 sugar equivalence (a single-expression branch is equivalent to `{ lift <expression> }`) at the level of OBSERVABLE RESULT. The two forms are NOT required to emit the same JavaScript (§17.6.8 grants IIFE/assign/ternary latitude) and in impl#1 they do not: the value-form lowers to a conditional expression, the explicit-lift form to a lift-target accumulation. This case pins the RESULT equivalence, which is what §17.6.10 asserts.
rationale: §17.6.10 (S391, ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S371 "value-form b"): a control-flow statement that is the sole content of a markup `${…}` interpolation and whose every branch is exactly one expression SHALL be a value-form and SHALL render the selected branch's value into the interpolation's position; a branch body that is exactly one expression SHALL be equivalent to `{ lift <expression> }`. Before the S391 amendment the compiler implemented this but SPEC contradicted it in four places — §17.6.1's `arm-body ::= '{' statement* lift-stmt statement* '}'` (a `lift` was REQUIRED), §17.6.2's "arm body SHALL produce its result value via a `lift` statement", §17.6.2's "an arm body that does not contain a `lift` ... contributes `not`", and §10.1's "Each arm ... SHALL contain exactly one `lift` statement". This case pins the amended surface so the sugar cannot silently regress. No diagnostic is expected: the form is valid.
